items.title: Recognise how a narrative overturns an established expectation
items.prompt: Which expectation does the ending overturn?

stimuli.text: For three chapters, villagers warn that the creature in the tower hoards stolen gold. When the children enter, they find it repairing lost toys and waiting for their owners.

options.label: The feared creature is expected to be a selfish thief but is shown to help others.
The tower is expected to be tall but turns out to be low.
The children are expected to find toys and find exactly that.

hints: Read the question again. What information do you have?
Try a smaller example or explore the idea with a grown-up.
items.explanation: The ending reverses the repeatedly established judgement of the creature.

items.title: Recognise how a narrative overturns an established expectation
items.prompt: Which expectation does the ending overturn?

stimuli.text: The narrator praises the champion’s honesty throughout the contest. At the end, a recording reveals that the narrator has been hiding the champion’s cheating.

options.label: The contest is revealed never to have taken place.
The supposedly reliable account is exposed as misleading.
The champion becomes honest because of the praise.

hints: Read the question again. What information do you have?
Try a smaller example or explore the idea with a grown-up.
items.explanation: New evidence challenges the trust placed in the narrator’s earlier account.

items.title: Recognise how a narrative overturns an established expectation

stimuli.text: Every practice scene shows the loud captain solving the team’s puzzles. In the final test, the overlooked reserve notices the crucial pattern and leads the solution.

options.label: The puzzles are shown to have no answers.

The expected problem-solver gives way to someone the team has overlooked.

hints: Read the question again. What information do you have?
Try a smaller example or explore the idea with a grown-up.
items.explanation: The resolution changes who the reader expects to provide the decisive insight.

items.title: Recognise how a narrative overturns an established expectation

hints: Read the question again. What information do you have?

items.title: Recognise how a narrative overturns an established expectation

stimuli.text: The printer ran out of paper, which stopped the notices being printed. Because no notices were ready, the office delayed their delivery. A new paper supply allowed printing and delivery to resume.

The printer runs out of paper.
Delivery is delayed because the notices are not ready.

hints: Read the question again. What information do you have?
Try a smaller example or explore the idea with a grown-up.
items.explanation: The missing paper causes a printing delay, which then causes the delivery delay.

items.title: Trace a cause-effect chain across clauses
items.prompt: Put the linked causes and effects in the order described.

stimuli.text: A blocked drain left water on the court. The slippery surface forced the match to pause. After the drain was cleared, the water drained away and the match resumed.

items.label: The slippery court causes a pause in the match.
Clearing the drain lets the court drain and the match resume.

hints: Read the question again. What information do you have?
Try a smaller example or explore the idea with a grown-up.
items.explanation: The sequence traces the physical cause through the pause to the repair that removes it.

items.title: Trace a cause-effect chain across clauses
items.prompt: Put the linked causes and effects in the order described.

stimuli.text: The label came off the seed tray, so the class could no longer identify its planting date. That missing date made the growth record incomplete. The teacher found the date in a photograph and the class completed the record.

items.label: A photograph supplies the date and the record is completed.
The label comes off the tray.
The missing date leaves a gap in the growth record.
The planting date can no longer be identified from the tray.

hints: Read the question again. What information do you have?
Try a smaller example or explore the idea with a grown-up.
items.explanation: The loss of identifying information creates the record gap; recovering the date resolves that gap.

items.title: Trace a cause-effect chain across clauses
items.prompt: Put the linked causes and effects in the order described.

stimuli.text: Strong wind loosened the tent pegs. The loose pegs allowed one side of the tent to sag. The team secured the pegs again, restoring the side’s support.

items.label: One side of the tent sags.
The loosened pegs provide less support.
Securing the pegs restores the support.

hints: Read the question again. What information do you have?
Try a smaller example or explore the idea with a grown-up.
items.explanation: Each step explains the next: loosening reduces support, reduced support permits sagging, and securing restores support.

items.title: Trace a cause-effect chain across clauses
items.prompt: Why did the group wait at the old stop?

stimuli.text: The corrected timetable reached the class after it had left. As a result, the group waited at the old stop and missed the relocated bus.

The new stop was necessarily farther away.
The correction arrived after the group had left.

hints: Read the question again. What information do you have?
Try a smaller example or explore the idea with a grown-up.
items.explanation: The text explicitly links the late information to the group’s use of the old stop.

items.title: Trace a cause-effect chain across clauses
items.prompt: What caused the builders to attach the shelf before its support?

stimuli.text: One line was omitted from the instructions. Without it, the builders attached the shelf before its support. The unsupported shelf tilted, so they had to undo that step.

options.label: A needed line was missing from the instructions.
Undoing the step removed the original instruction.
The shelf tilted before any building began.

hints: Read the question again. What information do you have?
Try a smaller example or explore the idea with a grown-up.
items.explanation: The omitted instruction is the earlier cause; tilting and reworking happen afterwards.

items.title: Trace a cause-effect chain across clauses
items.prompt: Which link directly explains why the ink spread?

hints: Read the question again. What information do you have?

items.explanation: The wet paper links the leaking box to the blurred ink; the difficulty reading is a later effect.

items.title: Trace a cause-effect chain across clauses

stimuli.text: A new sign directed visitors to the side entrance. More visitors used that entrance, so the queue at the front became shorter.

Every visitor stopped coming to the building.

hints: Read the question again. What information do you have?
Try a smaller example or explore the idea with a grown-up.
items.explanation: The sign changes where visitors enter, which reduces the number waiting at the front.

items.title: Trace a cause-effect chain across clauses
